line_items.reasoning: JPM guided full-year 2024 NII to ~$92.5B and NII ex Markets to ~$91.5B; Q4 results contributed to a full-year revenue of $173B with strong Markets (+21% YoY), IB fees (+49% YoY), and AWM performance, all pointing to NII and total revenue coming in at or above the raised guidance targets.

line_items.line_item: other (NII ex Markets run rate & 2025 outlook)
line_items.reasoning: Q3 guidance implied Q4 NII ex Markets would fall ~6% sequentially and flagged $87B as 'a little toppy' for 2025 consensus; instead, JPM guided 2025 NII ex Markets to ~$90B — above the $87B level they called toppy — suggesting Q4 NII ex Markets held up better than the implied sequential decline signaled.

Q3 guidance set 2024 adjusted expenses at ~$91.5B and flagged 2025 stepping up meaningfully above a ~$90B base; the actual 2025 expense guide came in at ~$95B, which is a more aggressive step-up than the language 'meaningfully above ~$90B' implied, representing a worse-than-guided cost trajectory.

JPM guided the 2024 Card net charge-off rate to remain ~3.4%, but Q4 Card NCOs rose to $2.1B with a 2025 NCO rate now guided at ~3.6%, indicating credit losses came in worse than the reaffirmed 3.4% target and the deterioration trend exceeded prior guidance.
